papers.title: Hantavirus in Dentistry: Occupational Exposure Considerations and a Proposed Tiered Infection Prevention and Control Framework-A Narrative Review.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Objective The aim of this study is to synthesize evidence on hantavirus transmission and occupational exposure pathways relevant to dentistry, and to propose an evidence‐informed tiered infection prevention and control (IPC) framework that distinguishes established from theoretical risk. Material and Methods The initial narrative search covered database inception through May 15, 2026 in MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, Google Scholar, and WHO/CDC/ECDC/OSHA sources, followed by a targeted PubMed/MEDLINE and public‐health guidance update through August 18, 2026. Approximately 1450 records were identified. After duplicate removal, 1070 records were subjected to title/abstract screening, 215 full‐text records were assessed for eligibility, and 45 sources were included in the final synthesis, comprising 34 peer‐reviewed publications and 11 gray‐literature or public‐health guidance sources. Results Environmental exposure to infected‐rodent contamination is the established occupational pathway. Limited person‐to‐person transmission is documented for the Andes virus (ANDV), but no dental transmission has been reported. ANDV RNA and culture‐based infectivity have been demonstrated in some oral/respiratory fluids; however, dental‐aerosol transmission has not been shown. Dental‐specific occupational risk therefore remains unquantified. Conclusions No dental transmission has been documented, and patient‐related risk remains uncertain. Standard precautions and rodent control are foundational; suspected or confirmed ANDV warrants transmission‐based precautions and airborne precautions for aerosol‐generating procedures according to current guidance. The proposed dental tiers are evidence‐informed, author‐derived, and unvalidated.

analysis.summary_en: Background: The review aims to synthesize evidence on hantavirus transmission pathways relevant to dentistry and to propose an evidence‑informed tiered IPC framework. Future research: Validation of the IPC tiers and quantitative risk assessments in dental settings are required.

papers.title_zh: 汉坦病毒 在牙科:职业暴露考虑及提出的分层感染预防与控制框架——叙述性综述。

analysis_zh.background: 本综述旨在综合关于汉坦病毒在牙科中的传播途径的证据,并提出基于证据的分层感染预防与控制框架。
analysis_zh.main_directions: 研究将环境啮齿动物暴露作为已确立的职业途径,探讨安第斯病毒有限的人际传播,并建议在牙科气溶胶产生程序中采用标准和基于传播的预防措施。
analysis_zh.current_state: 环境啮齿动物污染已被确认为职业传播途径;安第斯病毒显示有限的人际传播,但尚未记录牙科传播;牙科环境中的患者相关风险仍不确定。
analysis_zh.gaps: 牙科特定职业风险的幅度尚未量化,所提出的分层IPC框架尚未得到验证。
analysis_zh.future_research: 需要验证分层IPC框架,并开展针对汉坦病毒的牙科暴露风险定量研究。

papers.title: [Andes virus aboard the MV Hondius: Transnational public health challenges in ocean-going cruise travel].
papers.abstract: This article analyzes the cluster of Andes virus infections that occurred aboard the expedition vessel MV Hondius during a transatlantic crossing. Drawing on publicly available information released by the World Health Organization, the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control, and the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, it examines the key characteristics of this event: probable exposure in a natural reservoir area in South America before embarkation, limited human-to-human transmission in a closed maritime environment, difficulties in early case recognition, and the complexity of international contact tracing. The analysis shows that the vessel itself was not the source of the virus, but rather a setting in which public health risks were amplified due to prolonged cohabitation, limited onboard medical resources, and the cross-border mobility of passengers. Finally, the article highlights the importance of stratified contact management, timely reporting, effective international cooperation, and clear risk communication to avoid both underestimation of the risk and unnecessary public panic.

analysis.summary_en: Background: This article analyzes a cluster of Andes virus infections on the MV Hondius during a transatlantic cruise, a transnational public‑health challenge. Methods: The authors reviewed publicly available WHO, ECDC, and CDC reports describing likely exposure in a South American reservoir area before embarkation. Results: The vessel was not the virus source; prolonged cohabitation, limited onboard medical capacity, and cross‑border passenger movement amplified risk. Contribution: The work stresses stratified contact management, rapid reporting, international cooperation, and clear risk communication to prevent risk underestimation and public panic. Limitations: Only an abstract is provided; no primary data or quantitative details are reported.

papers.title_zh: [安第斯病毒] 在MV Hondius号船上:跨国海上邮轮旅行中的公共卫生挑战

analysis_zh.background: 本文分析了在跨大西洋航行期间,探险船 MV Hondius 上发生的 安第斯病毒 感染聚集事件。
analysis_zh.methods: 作者利用世界卫生组织、欧洲疾病预防控制中心和美国疾病控制与预防中心公开发布的信息,审查了在登船前可能发生于南美自然宿主区的暴露以及船上随后发生的事件。
analysis_zh.results: 分析表明,船只本身并非病毒来源;相反,长期同居、船上医疗资源有限以及乘客跨境流动加大了公共卫生风险。
analysis_zh.contribution: 本文强调分层接触管理、及时报告、有效的国际合作以及明确的风险沟通的重要性,以避免风险低估和不必要的公众恐慌。
analysis_zh.limitations: 仅提供摘要;未报告原始数据、详细流行病学信息、样本量及定量结果。

papers.summary_zh: 背景：本文分析了在跨大西洋航行期间,探险船 MV Hondius 上发生的 安第斯病毒 感染聚集事件。 方法：作者利用世界卫生组织、欧洲疾病预防控制中心和美国疾病控制与预防中心公开发布的信息,审查了在登船前可能发生于南美自然宿主区的暴露以及船上随后发生… 结果：分析表明,船只本身并非病毒来源;相反,长期同居、船上医疗资源有限以及乘客跨境流动加大了公共卫生风险。 贡献：本文强调分层接触管理、及时报告、有效的国际合作以及明确的风险沟通的重要性,以避免风险低估和不必要的公众恐慌。 局限：仅提供摘要;未报告原始数据、详细流行病学信息、样本量及定量结果。
